items.title: Almost-additive sequences have a normalized limit
items.statement: Let $(a_n)_{n\ge1}$ be a real sequence for which there is a finite constant $K$ with $|a_n|\le Kn$ for every $n\ge1$. Suppose there is a finite constant $C\ge0$ such that $|a_{m+n}-a_m-a_n|\le C$ for all positive integers $m,n$. Then $a_n/n$ has a finite limit as $n\to\infty$.
items.strategy: Shift by ±C to obtain subadditive and superadditive sequences, apply the sourced Fekete limit lemma to each, and use their vanishing normalized gap to conclude.

items.title: Finite MDP with bounded real rewards
items.statement: Let $S$ be a finite nonempty state set and let $A(s)$ be a finite nonempty action set for each $s\in S$, as in the finite-MDP convention. Put $D=\{(s,a):s\in S,\ a\in A(s)\}$ with its discrete sigma-algebra. Equip $S$ with its power-set sigma-algebra, $[0,1]$ with its Borel sigma-algebra, and $S\times[0,1]$ with the product sigma-algebra. A finite MDP with bounded real rewards specifies a probability kernel $Q$ from $D$ to $S\times[0,1]$; equivalently, each admissible $(s,a)$ has a probability measure $Q(\cdot\mid s,a)$ on that product measurable space. The reward-coordinate projection $(s',\rho)\mapsto\rho$ is measurable because the preimage of each Borel set $B\subseteq[0,1]$ is the product rectangle $S\times B$. Define the next-state law by $P(s'\mid s,a)=Q(\{s'\}\times[0,1]\mid s,a)$ and the mean reward by $r(s,a)=\int_{S\times[0,1]}\rho\,Q(ds',d\rho\mid s,a)\in[0,1]$. At each time, conditional on the observed history and the selected action, the next-state/reward pair has this law. Assume the Axiom of Choice for the path-space construction under policies.

items.title: Extended value iteration for a confidence set
items.statement:
Input finite nonempty state and action sets, upper reward estimates $\widetilde r(s,a)$, empirical transition laws $\widehat P(\cdot\mid s,a)$, nonnegative transition radii $b_p(s,a)$, a tolerance $\varepsilon>0$, and fixed orders of the states and actions for tie-breaking. For a vector $v\in\mathbb R^S$, write $\operatorname{span}(v)=\max_s v(s)-\min_s v(s)$ and let $\Delta(S)$ be the probability simplex on $S$. Initialize $u_0(s)=0$. At iteration $i\ge1$, compute
$$u_i(s)=\max_{a\in A(s)}\left[\widetilde r(s,a)+\max_{q\in\Delta(S):\|q-\widehat P(\cdot\mid s,a)\|_1\le b_p(s,a)}q\cdot u_{i-1}\right].$$
For every state-action pair $(s,a)$, run the following transfer routine using $v=u_{i-1}$. Put $q=\widehat P(\cdot\mid s,a)$, $c=\min\{1,b_p(s,a)/2\}$, and order the states $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ by nondecreasing $v(x_j)$, using the fixed state order to break ties. Set $j=1$ and $\ell=m$. While $c>0$ and $j<\ell$, advance $j$ while $q(x_j)=0$, then decrease $\ell$ while $j<\ell$ and $q(x_\ell)=1$. If $j\ge\ell$, stop. If $v(x_j)\ge v(x_\ell)$, stop. Otherwise set $d=\min\{c,q(x_j),1-q(x_\ell)\}$, replace $q(x_j)$ by $q(x_j)-d$ and $q(x_\ell)$ by $q(x_\ell)+d$, and replace $c$ by $c-d$; repeat. Call the resulting vector $q_{i,s,a}$.

For each state, compute $B_i(s,a)=\widetilde r(s,a)+q_{i,s,a}\cdot u_{i-1}$ for every action, record the first action $a_i(s)$ in the fixed action order attaining $\max_{a\in A(s)}B_i(s,a)$, and set $q_i(\cdot\mid s)=q_{i,s,a_i(s)}$. If $\operatorname{span}(u_i-u_{i-1})<\varepsilon$, return the stationary deterministic policy $\pi_i(s)=a_i(s)$, its corresponding transition rows $q_i$, the vector $u_{i-1}$ used in that backup, and the iteration index. Otherwise continue. The procedure is partial unless a separate termination result applies.

items.title: Communicating MDP and diameter
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the policy path laws used in the expectations below. For a finite MDP with bounded rewards, a policy assigns a probability distribution on $A(s)$ to each finite observed history ending in state $s$, with each action probability a measurable function of the history; deterministic policies are included. For states $x,y$, start at $S_0=x$ and define $\tau_y=\inf\{t\ge0:S_t=y\}$, with $\tau_y=+\infty$ if $y$ is never hit. This is an extended nonnegative measurable random variable because $\{\tau_y\le n\}=\bigcup_{t=0}^n\{S_t=y\}$. Take the expectation and the infimum over policies in $[0,+\infty]$. The MDP is communicating if $\inf_\pi\mathbb E_x^\pi[\tau_y]<\infty$ for every ordered pair $(x,y)$. Its raw diameter is $D_0=\sup_{x,y}\inf_\pi\mathbb E_x^\pi[\tau_y]$ in $[0,+\infty]$, and its normalized diameter is $D=\max\{1,D_0\}$ in the extended order. Since $S$ is finite, $D_0$ is finite for every communicating MDP. Thus a one-state MDP has $D_0=0$ and $D=1$.

items.title: Adaptive MDP visits admit fixed sample tapes
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the path-space construction. Fix a finite-horizon interaction of length $T$ in a finite MDP with bounded rewards and any nonanticipating policy: each action distribution is a measurable function of the revealed history, and policy randomization is independent of unexposed MDP samples. On an enlarged probability space with the same law for the observed interaction, for each admissible pair $(s,a)$ there is a sequence $Z_{s,a,1},\ldots,Z_{s,a,T}$ of independent samples with common law $Q(\cdot\mid s,a)$ such that the $j$th observed next-state/reward pair at $(s,a)$ is $Z_{s,a,j}$ whenever that visit occurs.

items.title: Termination of extended value iteration under communicating assumptions
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice for the path laws in the concluding UCRL2 application. For any finite nonempty state/action system, probability-vector empirical centers, finite nonnegative transition radii, and real value vector, the transfer routine in extended value iteration returns a feasible vector maximizing the value-vector expectation over the stated $\ell^1$ confidence set; it uses at most $2|S|+1$ positive transfers per row. If the upper rewards are finite, the tolerance is $\varepsilon>0$, and every transition radius is strictly positive, extended value iteration terminates. With fixed state and action orders, its returned policy, transition rows, value vector, and stopping index are measurable functions of the real input estimates. More precisely, write $F$ for its optimistic Bellman operator, put $\eta=\min_{s,a}\min\{1,b_p(s,a)/2\}>0$, and set $u_0=0$, $u_i=F(u_{i-1})$. Then
$$\operatorname{span}(u_i-u_{i-1})\le(1-\eta)^{i-1}\operatorname{span}(u_1),\qquad i\ge1.$$
When $\eta=1$, the span is zero for $i\ge2$. In particular, the positive UCRL2 confidence radii give finite stopping with tolerance $1/\sqrt{t_k}$ in every episode of a finite communicating MDP, including episodes whose confidence set misses the true model.
items.strategy: Decompose each positive L1 ball into a common positive mass and a residual subprobability; prove a span contraction and geometric decay.

items.title: Uniform empirical reward and transition confidence bounds
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice for the path-law, conditional-expectation, and martingale suppliers. Let a finite MDP have $S\ge1$ states and at most $A\ge1$ actions per state, and let $T\ge1$ be an integer and $\delta\in(0,1)$. Consider any length-$T$ interaction generated by a nonanticipating policy whose action distributions are measurable functions of the revealed history and whose randomization is independent of unexposed MDP samples. For each state-action pair $(s,a)$, whenever it has received $n$ visits by time $T$, let $\widehat r_n(s,a)$ be the mean of those first $n$ rewards and let $\widehat P_n(\cdot\mid s,a)$ be the empirical law of those next states. With probability at least $1-\delta$, simultaneously for all such pairs and all $1\le n\le T$,
$$|\widehat r_n(s,a)-r(s,a)|\le\sqrt{\frac{7\log(4SAT/\delta)}{2n}},\qquad \|\widehat P_n(\cdot\mid s,a)-P(\cdot\mid s,a)\|_1\le\sqrt{\frac{14S\log(4AT/\delta)}{n}},$$
where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
items.strategy: Apply Azuma–Hoeffding to fixed tape prefixes, convert transition ℓ1 error to a maximum over subsets, and union over pairs and sample counts.

items.title: Communicating MDPs have a common optimal average reward
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the path-law and conditional-expectation constructions. For a finite communicating MDP with rewards in $[0,1]$, let $V_n(s)$ be the supremum of the expected sum of the first $n$ rewards over all history-dependent policies starting from state $s$. For every state $s$, the limit $\lim_{n\to\infty}V_n(s)/n$ exists, is independent of $s$, and belongs to $[0,1]$.
items.strategy: Bound the finite-horizon value span by the diameter using a target-hitting policy, then show the maximum values are almost additive and invoke the proved normalized-limit lemma.

items.title: UCRL2 for finite communicating MDPs
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice for the interaction path law. The learner is given a finite nonempty state set $\mathcal S$, a finite nonempty action set $A(s)$ for each $s\in\mathcal S$, the observed initial state $s_1\in\mathcal S$, a horizon $T\ge1$, a confidence parameter $\delta\in(0,1)$, and fixed orders of the states and each state's actions. Let $S=|\mathcal S|$ and $A=\max_{s\in\mathcal S}|A(s)|$. Its unknown environment is a finite communicating MDP on $\mathcal S$ and these action sets with rewards in $[0,1]$; the transition kernel, reward laws, and their means are not inputs to the learner. At interaction $t$, the learner observes the current state $S_t$, chooses an admissible action, and then observes the realized reward $\rho_t$ and next state $S_{t+1}$.

Initialize $t=1$ and $S_1=s_1$. At the start $t_k$ of episode $k$, let $N_k(s,a)$ be the total number of visits to $(s,a)$ before $t_k$. If $N_k(s,a)>0$, let $\widehat r_k(s,a)$ be the mean of the rewards observed on those visits and $\widehat P_k(\cdot\mid s,a)$ their empirical next-state law. If $N_k(s,a)=0$, set $\widehat r_k(s,a)=0$ and set $\widehat P_k(\cdot\mid s,a)$ to the point mass at the first state in the fixed state order. Put $n_k(s,a)=\max\{1,N_k(s,a)\}$ and
$$b^r_k(s,a)=\sqrt{\frac{7\log(2SAt_k/\delta)}{2n_k(s,a)}},\qquad b^p_k(s,a)=\sqrt{\frac{14S\log(2At_k/\delta)}{n_k(s,a)}}.$$
Set $\widetilde r_k(s,a)=\min\{1,\widehat r_k(s,a)+b^r_k(s,a)\}$. Run extended value iteration with these estimates/radii and tolerance $1/\sqrt{t_k}$, obtaining a stationary deterministic policy $\pi_k$. Set every within-episode count $v_k(s,a)=0$ and execute the following loop. While $t\le T$, observe $S_t$, choose $a_t=\pi_k(S_t)$, observe $\rho_t$ and $S_{t+1}$, increment $v_k(S_t,a_t)$ and the all-history count for $(S_t,a_t)$, record this reward/transition observation, and retain the observed next state as the current state for the next interaction. Increment $t$ by one. End the episode immediately after an interaction when its pair's count reaches $v_k(s,a)=\max\{1,N_k(s,a)\}$, where $N_k$ remains the episode-start count; if $t\le T$, begin the next episode, otherwise terminate. All action and transition-vector ties use the fixed orders.

items.title: Average reward and pathwise regret
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the path laws and conditional-expectation constructions used by the common-average-reward result. For a finite communicating MDP, let $\rho^*$ denote the common optimal average reward. The existence and independence of this value from the initial state are proved in the immediately cited theorem. Under any policy, write $R_T=\sum_{t=1}^T\rho_t$ for the realized cumulative reward over the first $T$ interactions. The pathwise regret is the random variable $\Delta_T=T\rho^*-R_T$. Its expected regret is $\mathbb E[\Delta_T]=T\rho^*-\mathbb E[R_T]$. The pathwise random variable and its expectation are distinct objects.

items.title: UCRL2 high-probability pathwise regret bound
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice for the path-law and martingale suppliers. Let a finite communicating MDP have $S\ge1$ states, at most $A\ge1$ actions per state, rewards in $[0,1]$, and normalized diameter $D$. For each initial state, integer horizon $T\ge2$, and $\delta\in(0,1)$, UCRL2 with confidence parameter $\delta$ satisfies
$$\Pr\!\left(\Delta_T\le34DS\sqrt{AT\log(T/\delta)}\right)\ge1-\delta.$$
For every integer $T\ge1$, the same algorithm also satisfies
$$\Pr\!\left(\Delta_T\le34DS\sqrt{AT\log(2T/\delta)}\right)\ge1-\delta.$$
Here $\Delta_T=T\rho^*-R_T$ is realized, pathwise regret and logarithms are natural. These are assertions for each fixed horizon and initial state. The original formula with $\log(T/\delta)$ and $T\ge1$ is false, as refuted below.
items.strategy: Use fixed-tape anytime confidence, the local EVI contraction, finite-horizon span control, predictable martingale increments, count doubling, and explicit constants; refute the exact original T=1 formula.

items.title: Expected regret lower bound for communicating MDPs
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited by the probability and Pinsker suppliers. Here a learning algorithm is not given the unknown MDP's reward or transition laws and, at each time, uses a fixed measurable probability kernel from the observed finite history to the admissible actions, the same kernel in every environment; its action randomization is independent of unexposed MDP samples. For all integers $S,A\ge10$, all real $D\ge\max\{1,20\log_A S\}$, all integers $T\ge DSA$, every such learning algorithm, and every prescribed initial state label, there exists a finite communicating MDP with exactly $S$ states including that label, exactly $A$ actions in each state, rewards in $[0,1]$, and normalized diameter at most $D$, such that the algorithm's expected regret from that initial state satisfies
$$\mathbb E[T\rho^*-R_T]\ge0.015\sqrt{DSAT}.$$
The MDP may depend on the algorithm, parameters, and prescribed initial state. The original planned statement with reversed minimax quantifiers and no feasibility condition $D\ge1$ is false; it is retained and refuted below.
items.strategy: Prove the corrected minimax constant by an exact-state/action two-state-pair tree and separate small-diameter bandit construction, with finite-history KL/Pinsker and complete constant transfer; refute original infeasible scope.

items.title: A noncommunicating MDP can have state-dependent average reward
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the path laws in the communicating-MDP definition. Let $S=\{0,1\}$ and let each state have one action. Both states are absorbing. The reward is always $0$ in state $0$ and always $1$ in state $1$. The MDP is not communicating, and its long-run average reward is $0$ from initial state $0$ and $1$ from initial state $1$.

items.title: One-state MDP and normalized diameter
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the path-law and common-average-reward suppliers. Let $S=\{s\}$, $A(s)=\{a\}$, let the transition return to $s$ with probability one, and let every reward equal $1$. Then the MDP is communicating, its raw diameter is $D_0=0$, its normalized diameter is $D=1$, its optimal average reward is $1$, and its unique policy has regret $0$ at every horizon.

items.title: A random reward separates pathwise and expected regret
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the path-law and common-average-reward suppliers. Let there be one state and one action, with deterministic self-transition and independent Bernoulli$(1/2)$ rewards. This MDP is communicating. Then $\rho^*=1/2$. At horizon $T=1$, pathwise regret equals $1/2$ when the reward is $0$ and equals $-1/2$ when the reward is $1$, although expected regret is $0$.
